newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN DATA DUE - German industry output in 1997.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN DATA DUE - German industry output in 1997.

text.p: The German Economics Ministry, in a move to bring its statistical reporting into line with other rich nations, on Thursday published a timetable for the release of monthly industrial output data for the rest of 1997.
The ministry said the schedule fulfilled a commitment made at the end of last year to meet standards of statistical reporting set by the International Monetary Fund.

But it warned that, despite efforts to meet the timetable, it could not rule out delays because of the devolved structure of Germany's gathering of statistics and the time needed by the Bundesbank to calculate seasonal adjustments.

Separate industrial orders data do not fall under the minimum IMF standards, and no advanced release schedule will be published. The ministry typically announces it will publish the data an hour or so before their release.
